title: bug: stale reaper auto-closes active extmsg Slack room groups, freezing inbound transcripts
body:
## Summary

The stale-bead reaper can auto-close active external-message room group roots. The Slack adapter continues receiving provider events, but canonical transcript state stops advancing and session-bound replies can fail until the room is rebound.

## Live evidence (Thunderfart City, 2026-09-15 UTC)

- Mayor room `C0BQ0UXGBV5` referenced group root `th-9yy3`, auto-closed by the reaper on 2026-09-14 (`stale:auto-closed by reaper`). Its canonical transcript froze at sequence 170 even though the adapter logged later inbound events.
- Dom room `C0BRAMAFTDE` referenced group root `th-99k3`, closed the same way. Its transcript froze at sequence 404; two human messages remained visible in Slack provider history but did not reach `champagne/dom`.
- A control room whose group root remained open continued to ingest normally.
- Rebinding created open roots `th-jo50l` (Mayor) and `th-20g7o` (Dom), plus active direct bindings. Dom then received the recovered request, published a reply, and two later human messages ingested successfully.

## Expected

Active extmsg group roots, participant records, binding records, and transcript/state beads must not be considered disposable stale work. Reaper eligibility should exclude these durable protocol records.

## Acceptance

- Exclude active extmsg protocol records from stale auto-close.
- Add a regression test that advances time beyond the reaper threshold, runs the reaper, and proves an active room group/binding remains open and subsequent inbound advances the canonical transcript.
- If a referenced group is already closed or missing, inbound should fail visibly and/or self-heal instead of logging apparent acceptance while dropping canonical delivery.

This is separate from `slack-full` handling of Slack `file_share` subtype events.

title: fix(api): an output turn carries the entry id its cursors need
body:
## Summary

The agent output endpoints accept `before`/`after` entry-ID cursors and report `has_older_messages`, but `OutputTurn` carries no ID. A client can be told older messages exist while holding nothing valid to send as a cursor. This adds the entry ID to every turn.

Hand-written diff is 30 lines across three files: `handler_agent_output.go` (+4), `handler_agent_output_turns.go` (+2), and a local test (+24). The other 29 files in the list are regenerated artifacts — see below.

## Problem

`OutputTurn` on `main` is:

```go
Role      string `json:"role"`
Text      string `json:"text"`
Timestamp string `json:"timestamp,omitempty"`
```

The paging contract is advertised and unusable in the same response: `has_older_messages` tells a client to page backwards, the handlers accept an entry-ID cursor to do it with, and nothing in the payload is that ID. An invented ID answers 500, so the only workable client behavior is to not page at all.

## Fix

Thread the ID onto all three paths that produce a turn:

- `entryToTurn` — the paged read and the live stream, from `TranscriptEntry.UUID`
- `historyEntryToTurn` — the history path, from `HistoryEntry.ID`

Both sources already carried the identifier; only the serialized struct omitted it. The field is additive and omitted when empty, so a client that ignores it is unaffected.

## Why the field is optional

`id` is `omitempty` deliberately, not defensively. `TranscriptEntry` is an alias for `sessionlog.Entry`, so the value is the raw provider UUID — and the paging layer matches on exactly that: `uniqueEntryIDs` (`internal/sessionlog/pagination.go:135`) skips any entry whose `UUID` is empty when it builds the set of valid cursors.

So an entry with no provider UUID is not addressable as a cursor at all, and that predates this change. Omitting the field is the honest signal for that turn. The two alternatives are both worse:

- Emitting `id: ""` advertises a cursor value the paging layer explicitly refuses to index.
- Minting a synthesized ID (the normalizer does this for its own `Provenance.Derived` bookkeeping) would produce a value `uniqueEntryIDs` still skips, so `before=<synthesized>` would 500 — the exact failure this PR exists to remove.

If you would rather every turn be addressable, that is a change to what the cursor index accepts rather than to this serialization, and I would send it separately.

## A consumer, in the same PR

`SessionPeek` keyed its turn list by array index. A list that pages *backwards* prepends older turns, so on every page-back React rebound each existing turn to a different DOM node and any per-node state followed the wrong turn. It now prefers the entry id, matching the pattern already used in `StructuredTranscript.tsx` (`key={message.id !== '' ? message.id : index}`).

The new test in `SessionPeek.render.test.tsx` discriminates rather than decorates: it captures the node holding a turn, prepends an older turn, and asserts that node still holds the same turn. Reverted to `key={idx}` it fails with `expected '#02··assistantalpha' to contain 'beta'`, which is precisely the rebinding bug.

## Regeneration

`OutputTurn` is `additionalProperties: false` and Huma derives the schema from the Go struct, so a hand-edited spec would make the response invalid against itself. Everything derived is regenerated rather than edited:

```
go run ./cmd/genspec
PATH="$(go env GOPATH)/bin:$PATH" go generate ./internal/api/genclient
npm run generate:client   # in internal/api/dashboardspa/web
make dashboard-build
```

That accounts for `internal/api/openapi.json`, the `docs/reference/schema` mirrors, `internal/api/genclient/client_gen.go`, the dashboard's typed client (`types.gen.ts`, `zod.gen.ts`), and the embedded `internal/api/dashboardspa/dist/` bundle whose asset hashes move with it. A fresh `go run ./cmd/genspec` on this branch produces no further diff.

## Evidence from a running deployment

This has been serving on our fork's supervisor since 2026-09-10. Against that build:

```
$ curl -s ".../v0/city/<city>/agent/<agent>/output?tail=3" | jq -c '.turns[] | keys'
["id","role","text","timestamp"]
```

On stock `main` the same read returns `["role","text","timestamp"]`.

## Scope

Deliberately only the ID. An earlier revision of this branch also changed how a `tool_use` turn renders its input; that is a data-modeling question about `OutputTurn.Text` rather than a missing-ID bug, and it is being written up separately so it can be discussed on its own terms.

## Testing

- [x] `go test ./internal/api/ -run 'OutputTurn|AgentOutput|Turns|EntryToTurn' -count=1` — ok, 7.1s
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run src/components/SessionPeek.render.test.tsx` — 5 passed, including the new identity test; verified it fails when the key is reverted to the array index
- [x] `go run ./cmd/genspec` produces no further diff against the committed spec
- [x] `make dashboard-build` — bundle rebuilt and committed, so the embedded `dist/` is not stale
- [x] `fork-verify` on this head SHA — upstream's own fork workflow, `go build ./...` plus vet and unit suites on Linux
- [x] Verified live against a supervisor running this change (output above)
- [ ] `make check` — fails only on a finding that is not from this branch, verified: clean `upstream/main` fails identically on `cmd/gc/dolt_data_dir_lock_other.go:15:32` `unused-parameter` (revive), same `EXIT=2`
- [ ] `make test-integration` — not run

## Checklist

- [ ] Linked an issue — none filed; happy to if you'd prefer it tracked
- [x] Added or updated tests for behavior changes
- [x] Regenerated every derived artifact rather than hand-editing the schema
- [x] No breaking change: an additive, omit-when-empty field on an existing response

title: fix(mail): stop the pending-mail notice from naming a session bead id
body:
## Problem

The pending-mail notice interpolates the sender's resolved mail address:

```go
msg := fmt.Sprintf("You have mail from %s", sender)
```

A session with no alias addresses as its own session bead id
(`session.MailboxAddressFromInfo` falls back to `info.ID`), so the notice
reads exactly like a message id. Readers then ran `gc mail read
sc-wisp-p2yobus` and got nothing useful. This happened four times in one
mayor session on 2026-09-15: `sc-wisp-8fog4ni`, `sc-wisp-jvcub7t`,
`sc-wisp-p2yobus`, and `sc-wisp-zgm0eu9`, all `issue_type: session`, titled
`omp-4`, `omp-5`, `omp-1`, and `omp-1`.

The selection queries are not at fault: `gc mail check` and `gc mail inbox`
share one predicate and agree.

The damage half already landed — beadmail now refuses to read a non-message
bead. This is the other half: stop the notice from pointing at one.

## Change

- `mailNudgeNotice` renders the notice. The only id it names is the message
  id, which always addresses a bead of type message, and it appends the
  command that works: `gc mail read <id>`.
- `mailNudgeSenderLabel` probes the store instead of guessing from the shape
  of the string, because an alias (`omp-1`) and a bead id (`sc-gkq1b`) are
  the same shape. A sender that resolves to a bead is named by that bead's
  title; a titleless one is not named at all.
- `collapseMailNudges` folds two or more pending mail notices into a count
  and a pointer at the inbox. A reader facing several notices has no reason
  to open any particular one first. The collapse is display-only: the drain
  acks `queuedNudgeIDs(items)` from the original claimed slice, not this one.

Before:

```
- [mail] You have mail from sc-wisp-p2yobus
```

After, one message:

```
- [mail] You have mail from omp-1 (message gc-42) — run: gc mail read gc-42
```

After, several:

```
- [mail] You have 3 unread messages — run: gc mail inbox
```

## Tests

`cmd/gc/cmd_nudge_mail_notice_test.go`:

- `TestMailNudgeNoticeNeverNamesSessionBeadID` — the notice contains no
  session bead id and points at the message.
- `TestMailNudgeNoticeDropsUntitledSessionSender` — a session with no title
  is not named at all rather than named by id.
- `TestMailNudgeNoticeKeepsAliasSender` — an alias passes through, proving
  the decision is a store probe and not a shape heuristic.
- `TestMailNudgeNoticeNamesOnlyMessageBeads` — every id in the notice that
  resolves in the store is of type `message`.
- `TestQueuedMailNudgesCollapseToInbox` — three pending mail notices produce
  one summary naming none of the three ids, and the non-mail reminder
  survives.
- `TestSingleMailNudgeKeepsItsMessageID` — one pending message keeps its id.

Two existing assertions pinned the exact notice text
(`cmd_mail_test.go:2087` and `assertQueuedMailNudgeMessage`); both now assert
the prefix, so they still pin the sender contract without pinning the
suffix.

`go test ./cmd/gc/ -run 'Mail|Nudge'` passes. The `TestReapClosedBeadWorktrees_*`
and `TestDiscoverWorktreeLiveness_*` failures in the full package run are
environmental and pre-existing: a local PATH guard refuses
`git -c core.hooksPath`, which those tests use to build fixtures.

title: fix(supervisor): clear the launchd disable override on start
body:
## Problem

On macOS, `gc supervisor stop` runs `launchctl disable` against
`gui/<uid>/com.gascity.supervisor` (`cmd/gc/cmd_supervisor_lifecycle.go`,
`durablyStopSupervisorLaunchd`). `launchctl disable` writes a persistent
override to `/var/db/com.apple.xpc.launchd/disabled.<uid>.plist` that survives
logout and reboot.

The only code that clears that override is `supervisorLaunchctlRun("enable",
target)` inside `loadAndStartSupervisorLaunchd`, whose sole non-test caller is
the `gc supervisor install` path. `gc supervisor start` never called it; it
forked a bare `gc supervisor run` child.

So the ordinary stop-then-start cycle leaves a machine that reports healthy and
is not supervised. Observed on a real machine: after `gc supervisor start`,
`gc supervisor status --json` returned `running=true pid=1902` while
`launchctl print-disabled` reported the agent disabled and `launchctl print`
reported it not loaded. The supervisor survived only as a foreground process. A
logout or reboot would have left the city with no supervisor, with no warning
anywhere in gc's output.

## Fix

- `gc supervisor start` re-registers through launchd when the agent plist
  exists, reusing `loadAndStartSupervisorLaunchd` (enable, load, kickstart). It
  falls back to the forked child, with an explicit warning, when launchd
  refuses. The readiness wait moves into `waitForSupervisorStartResult` so both
  paths share it.
- `gc supervisor status` reports launchd supervision state. A disabled or
  unloaded agent adds `supervised: false` and `supervision_warning` to the JSON
  payload, and a stderr warning to the text output, instead of answering a bare
  `running: true`. The exit code does not change, so existing monitoring keeps
  working.
- `supervisorLaunchdDisabled` parses `launchctl print-disabled`. The value
  spelling changed across macOS releases (`=> true` on older systems,
  `=> disabled` on newer ones), so both are accepted.

The systemd path is untouched: `startSupervisorViaLaunchd` returns false on
every non-darwin platform before it touches `launchctl`, and a test pins that.

## Tests

`cmd/gc/cmd_supervisor_launchd_override_test.go`. A `fakeLaunchd` models the
override and the loaded state.

- `TestSupervisorStartClearsLaunchdOverrideAfterStop` runs the real
  stop-then-start cycle and asserts the override is absent and the agent is
  loaded. Fails before the fix, passes after.
- `TestSupervisorStatusJSONReportsDisabledLaunchdAgent` asserts status surfaces
  a disabled agent. Fails before the fix, passes after.
- `TestStartSupervisorViaLaunchdSkipsNonDarwin` and
  `TestStartSupervisorViaLaunchdSkipsUninstalledAgent` guard the systemd path
  and a Mac that never installed the service.
- `TestLaunchdPrintDisabledReportsDisabled` covers both value spellings and the
  absent-label case.
- `TestSupervisorLaunchdSupervisionWarning` covers healthy, disabled, and
  unloaded.

Verification: `go test ./cmd/gc/ -run 'Supervisor|Launchd|Systemd|Drift|Start'`
passes.

## Note on a third option

The issue also suggested dropping the persistent `disable` from stop and using
`bootout` alone. This PR keeps `disable`, because the stop path relies on it to
prevent launchd from immediately restarting a job it is told to boot out. The
asymmetry, not the `disable` itself, was the defect.

title: Five accepted limitations in the event-driven nudge dispatcher
body:
## What is true today

The event-driven nudge dispatcher in `cmd/gc/nudge_event_dispatcher.go` delivers
a queued nudge when the provider reports a session idle. It ships with five
known limitations, each reviewed and accepted before it shipped. This issue
exists so they outlive the pull request that introduced them.

## The limitations

**1. No per-delivery timeout.** `runtime.Provider.Nudge` takes no context and the
herdr client applies no default timeout. `passSlots` bounds how many deliveries
may start at once and the drain grace bounds how long shutdown waits, but
nothing bounds one delivery's own lifetime during normal operation. A session
whose pane wedges permanently leaves a goroutine parked in `Nudge` for the life
of the process, holding its captured store and provider handles. Each distinct
session that wedges once over a long-running controller adds one.

**2. A post-delivery stamp can land on a closed store.** Shutdown abandons a
wedged delivery after the drain grace and then closes storage. The abandoned
goroutine may still write. Whether that panics or silently drops depends on the
store's write-after-close behaviour, which this code does not establish as safe.
The dispatcher's own doc comment states this directly.

**3. A provider-changing reload is not fenced against an in-flight delivery.** In
`cmd/gc/city_runtime.go` the reload path calls `gracefulStopAll` before
re-pointing the dispatcher at the new provider. A delivery already inside
`Provider.Nudge` is not fenced against that stop on the same session, so the
queue entry can be acknowledged even though the agent never processed it.
This needs a provider-changing reload specifically, which is rarer than a
plain reload or a shutdown.

**4. The `gc prime` hook path constructs a session provider every time.**
`hookNudgePollerSessionProvider` in `cmd/gc/cmd_prime.go` is called
unconditionally on a hook-frequency path that the nudge dispatcher's own comment
says must stay latency-bounded. It fails open on error, which is the right
safety property, but the cost on the success path is unaddressed. Whether
`newSessionProviderFromContext` is cheap was not established.

**5. The shutdown check narrows a race rather than closing it.**
`acquirePassSlot` checks cancellation in a non-blocking `select` before racing
for a slot. Cancellation landing between that check and the racing select still
lets one call acquire a slot and run. This replaced a version with no
pre-check at all, where both cases were ready simultaneously and Go chose
pseudo-randomly: measured at 103 of 200 calls running when they should not have.
The sustained case is now 0 of 1000. What remains is a single call straddling
the instant of cancellation.

## What needs deciding

1. Whether 1 and 2 are one fix or two. A per-delivery timeout would bound the
   goroutine and remove the abandoned-writer window with it, which argues for
   one change. The counter-argument is that `Provider.Nudge` taking no context
   is an interface question, not a dispatcher one.
2. Whether 5 is worth closing. Re-checking cancellation after the slot is
   acquired and releasing it closes the window completely, at the cost of a
   second check on the hot path.
3. Whether 3 wants a fence or an acknowledgement check. Fencing the reload is
   heavier; having the delivery confirm the session is still on the expected
   provider before acknowledging is lighter but leaves a smaller window.

## Scope

Whichever shape wins: the dispatcher change, its test, and for 1 an interface
decision about whether `Provider.Nudge` should take a context, which reaches
every runtime provider rather than herdr alone.

title: fix(nudge): derive the CLI's session-class store from the city's work store at every call site
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #6348: the nudge CLI derived its session-class store from the nudges store rather than the city's own work store, so session reads miss on a city that relocates nudges alone. The issue named 4 call sites against an older revision; the current tree has grown to 9 -- found by grepping every `cliSessionStore`/`cliSessionFrontDoor` call in `cmd_nudge.go` rather than trusting the issue's own count, since the anti-pattern had clearly spread since it was filed.
- Fixed via the issue's own recommended option B: a new `cliSessionStoreForCity`/`cliNudgeSessionStore` pair that derives the session store from the city's own work store every time, ignoring whatever store a caller already holds open (preserving the nil->nil identity path some call sites deliberately rely on). All 9 sites now go through it.
- Also fixed a smaller issue found along the way: the poll loop was re-deriving the session store fresh on every delivery tick instead of reusing the value already computed once above the loop.

## Known limitation (disclosed, not papered over)
- The reporter's own repro (relocate nudges without sessions) could not actually be run against this build: the storage-composition gate currently refuses any `[storage]` arrangement short of "every class stays on work" or "every class moves to one shared binding together" -- confirmed by hand, that exact city.toml fails config load with "this build cannot serve" before ever reaching the bug. So this fix is real defensive correctness (matching what `tryDeliverQueuedNudgesByPoller`'s own doc comment already documents as the intended invariant), but it is not independently observable as a live bug today under any configuration this build currently allows.

## Test plan
- Regression test pins the only currently-reachable form of the invariant: on an ordinary single-store city, the session store must not depend on the store handle passed in as its base -- proven with a decoy store, verified failing on revert.

title: fix(config): let a template opt a cold pool out of the wake-probe's clamped-1 override (Agent.ColdWake)

## Summary
- Fixes #6351: a pool with a custom `scale_check` could not be held at zero by that check -- when it succeeded and returned 0, the cold-pool wake probe's own demand (clamped to at most 1) was merged over it by maximum, so `1 > 0` always won and the pool woke anyway, despite the clamp's own comment claiming this couldn't happen.
- Considered the issue's "option 1" (blanket-trust every successful custom check as authoritative) but rejected it: running the full existing suite first showed it would break `TestBuildDesiredState_ScaleFromZero_CrossRig` and three siblings, which deliberately rely on the wake probe overriding a check that returns 0 *because* the check is blind to demand from a store it never queries (e.g. a rig-scoped check that can't see city-store routed work).
- Built the issue's "option 2" instead: `Agent.ColdWake` (`cold_wake` in TOML, default unset/true = today's unchanged behavior). Only templates that explicitly opt out get the new "authoritative zero" behavior. Threaded through `AgentPatch`, `AgentOverride`, `Agent.Clone`, and regenerated OpenAPI/docs schema (which correctly cascaded into a dashboard SPA rebuild via the pre-commit hook catching the new field in the generated TS client).

## Test plan
- Regression test verified by reverting just the merge-condition line and confirming it fails with the exact reported symptom.
- Full `internal/config` suite + relevant `cmd/gc` suites: pass. `go vet`: clean.
- Zero modifications to pre-existing tests beyond one docstring update explaining why it still asserts the old (correct, unchanged-by-default) behavior.
